sections.h2: What does the Martin County, NC Register of Deeds handle?
sections.html:
The office records land documents, keeps their index and also issues vital records and marriage licenses. In Martin County, it sits on the first floor of the Martin County Governmental Building in Williamston, and the county's own page says the office has indexed instruments back to 1771.

For someone selling a house, the land side matters most. The office records deeds, easements, agreements, deeds of trust, assignments, releases and plats, and it keeps an index of plats. It also files uniform commercial code statements as fixture filings in the real estate books, a practice the county dates to July 1, 2001.

The same counter helps with military discharge records (DD-214s), notary oaths and assumed business names. Phone questions about records go to (252) 789-4320, the number the office prints for further information.

sections.h2: Can you search Martin County land records online?
sections.html:
Yes. The county page says deeds are available online at martinrod.org, and that the land records there go back to 1771. A vital records index online covers births and deaths from 1913 and marriages from 1882.

Searching the index before you list is a good habit for an inherited or long-held house. You can see the last deed into the owner, any deed of trust that was never cancelled, and any easement across the lot.

  • Look up your name and the name of the person you inherited from.
  • Read the legal description on the last deed and compare it with the tax record.
  • Check for old deeds of trust with no release recorded behind them.
  • Note any plat or recorded right of way that touches the parcel.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Martin County?
sections.html:
The county prints a fee list that matches the statewide statute: $26 for a deed or other instrument up to 15 pages and $4 for each page past 15. A deed of trust costs $64 for the first 35 pages plus $4 for each additional page or fraction.

Fees printed on the Martin County Register of Deeds page
ServiceFee
Deed or other instrument, first 15 pages$26
Deed of trust, first 35 pages$64
Plat or map, per page (18 x 24)$21.00
Certified copy, first page$5.00
Each additional certified page$2.00
Excise tax on deeds$2.00 per $1000 of price
Each additional instrument in one document$10.00
Cancellation or satisfaction of a deed of trustNo fee
Photocopy, uncertified$0.25 per page

The page carries a note that fees are subject to change, so confirm the amount before you send a check. Money orders are payable to Martin County Register of Deeds.

sections.h2: What format rules does a Martin County deed have to meet?
sections.html:
A deed must follow the layout rules in G.S. 161-10 or the office adds a $25.00 nonstandard document fee. Martin County lists the rules on its page for instruments signed on or after July 1, 2002.

  • Paper of 8 1/2 by 11 or 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • A blank margin of 3 inches at the top of the first page and half an inch on the other sides and on every later page.
  • Black type or print on white paper, no smaller than 9 points, on one side of the page only.
  • The type of instrument stated at the top of the first page.

Blanks may be completed in pen, and corrections may be made in pen. Exhibits and attachments must meet the same standards as the deed.

The rule applies by the date the instrument was signed, not the date it is presented.

sections.h2: Why does the recording order matter for a Martin County sale?
sections.html:
Registration time decides who comes first. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance, option, lease over three years or right of first refusal does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies.

In Martin County that means the Williamston office, even when you live out of state. If a creditor records a judgment before your buyer's deed reaches the counter, the buyer can be left behind it. Closing attorneys handle this by recording right after funds are confirmed.

  • Send the signed deed and any payoff release to the office together.
  • Bring a check or money order payable to Martin County Register of Deeds for the fees.
  • Keep the recording stamp page, which shows the book and page of your deed.

sections.h2: Who pays the Martin County deed transfer tax?
sections.html:
The seller pays. State law puts the excise tax on the transferor, payable to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. The statute sets it at $1.00 for each $500 or fractional part of the price or value.

Martin County's fee list prints the same rate as $2.00 per $1000, based on purchase price. Half of the money goes to the county general fund and half to the state, and the county may keep 2 percent of the state share.

Do not guess at the amount for your sale. Your closing attorney will put the exact figure on the settlement statement, and the register of deeds will not record the deed until it is paid.

sections.h2: How do Martin County deeds tie to the tax bill?
sections.html:
Recording a deed does not clear a tax bill. Martin County's tax collector mails bills for real and personal property in July or August, due September 1, and interest-free payment is allowed through January 5. A 2 percent penalty applies from January 6, and three-fourths of one percent interest accrues each month after that.

The collector's office is at 305 East Main Street, Room 125, in Williamston, and the phone is 252-789-4360. State law also requires the collector to advertise unpaid real estate taxes in the local paper between March 1 and June 30, and the page says the taxpayer bears an extra cost for that advertising.

If you are selling, get a payoff figure from the collector before closing so the bill is paid from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What is the market backdrop for a Martin County seller?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau reports a Martin County population of 21,601 on July 1, 2025, down 2.0 percent from the April 2020 estimates base. The county has 11,071 housing units, and the owner-occupied rate is 66.8 percent for 2020 to 2024.

The median value of an owner-occupied home was $109,700 for 2020 to 2024, with median household income of $48,578 in 2024 dollars. The Census Bureau recorded 0 building permits for 2025.

Older houses with deferred repairs are common in places with this profile, and a conventional buyer's lender may balk at them. A cash buyer can buy as-is and close once the deed is ready to record. Ask your attorney or title agent to run the land records first, so any old deed of trust is cancelled before closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Martin County Register of Deeds located?
faqs.a: It is on the first floor of the Martin County Governmental Building in Williamston. The county's page lists (252) 789-4320 for questions, and the county's government center is at 305 East Main Street.

faqs.q: How far back do Martin County deed records go?
faqs.a: They go back to 1771. The county page says deeds can be searched online at martinrod.org and that the office has indexed instruments since 1771.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed of trust in Martin County?
faqs.a: A deed of trust costs $64 for the first 35 pages plus $4 for each additional page or fraction. A deed or other ordinary instrument is $26 for the first 15 pages.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a mortgage satisfaction in Martin County?
faqs.a: No. The county lists cancellations, certificates of satisfaction and notices of satisfaction as no fee, which matches the state fee schedule.

faqs.q: Does the Martin County deed excise tax come from the buyer or seller?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. The county prints the rate as $2.00 per $1000 of purchase price, and the register of deeds collects it before recording the deed.
